output.name: Taresk

anatomy.part: crown corner, top of the kite
bottom point, where the tail is tied on

output.myth: Each winter a child who has come through it gets one knot tied in the tail of a kite, and Hesk the Reel keeps the count. Ennu the Kite-Wright made the first one for an old woman on the north shore who had lived through eighty-one winters and wanted it known. The knots were tight and close. Then Tavo came up the strait laughing, and the kite went up with its tail full and would not come down, and the old woman held the spool with cold hands and did not let go. Aun, who wants to know everything, flew up beside it and asked what the knots were for. Count them, she said, and you will know what you kept. Hesk tied the last knot herself, from the far side of the Reel. The kite is still aloft, very high, and every night the knots are counted by the children who look up and get them wrong.
output.verse:
Hesk counts each knot twice,
a knot for each winter kept,
the children miscount.
